slides.title: Nobody reads your campaign report. They read *the decisions*.
slides.subtitle: 3 prompts I use to turn charts into a one-page memo.

slides.label: 01 · The rule
slides.title: The sheet does the maths. AI does the words.
slides.body: Calculate every number in your spreadsheet first. Then paste the finished table and tell the AI: *do not recalculate anything*. That one rule removes most of the risk in AI reporting.

slides.label: 02 · The so-what pass
slides.title: Ask for decisions, not a summary.
slides.body: Prompt: *Using only this table, give me 3 decisions for next month: keep, change, stop. Each with the number behind it and one line on why.* Summaries describe. Decisions get read.

slides.label: 03 · The sceptic pass
slides.title: Let it argue like the CFO.
slides.body: Prompt: *Act as a sceptical finance lead. Which of these decisions would you challenge, and what number would you ask for?* Fix the weak ones before the meeting, not during it.

slides.label: 04 · The what-we-don't-know pass
slides.title: Say what the data can't prove.
slides.body: Prompt: *List what this data cannot tell us, and what we'd need to measure next time.* Clients trust a report more when it admits limits. I've seen that in every honest review.

slides.title: Save this before your next *client review*.
